units: <cite ref="Yoma 26a:5">Yoma 26ᵃ</cite> <he>הא שכיחא והא וכ׳</he> the one is a frequent (daily) performance, but the other is rare.
<cite ref="Berakhot 2a:13">Ber. 2ᵃ</cite> <he>והא קמ״ל</he> and this he intimates.
<cite ref="Berakhot 4b:13">Ib. 4ᵇ</cite> <he>והא דקאמרי וכ׳</he> and as to this (the fact) that they say, ‘Until midnight’, it is said in order to prevent &c.
<cite ref="Berakhot 9a:14">Ib. 9ᵃ</cite> <he>הא דר׳ אחא</he> as to this (opinion) of R. Aḥa.
Ib. 15ᵇ הא דידיה והא דרביה the one represents his own opinion, the other that of his teacher; a. v. fr.—הא והא both.
<cite ref="Taanit 25a:18">Taan. 25ᵃ</cite> bot.; a. fr.—Contractions: <he>הָנַיְחָא</he> = <he>הא ניחא</he> this would be right.
<cite ref="Yoma 3a">Yoma 3ᵃ</cite>; a. fr.—<he>וְהָדְתַנְיָא</he> = <he>והא דת׳</he> and as to it being taught in the Boraitha.
B. Kam. 12ᵃ; a. fr.—With prefixes: דְּהָא of this.
Yoma 13ᵇ דגיטא דהא וכ׳ that the letter of divorce for this wife is invalid; a. fr.—אַהָא = על הא referring to this.
<cite ref="Ketubot 40b:13">Keth. 40ᵇ</cite> <he>אַתּוּן אהא וכ׳</he> ye cited it (Resh Lakish’s opinion) with reference to that, we used to cite it with reference to this; a. fr.
<cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 22:7">Targ. Gen. XXII, 7</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 12a:18">B. Kam. 12ᵃ</cite> <he>הא עולא וכ׳</he> here is (the opinion of) Ulla, here &c.; a. fr.

senses.gloss: introducing a self-evident consequent, then of course.
units: Yoma 13ᵃ מיתה הך הא קיימא הא if that one dies, there is the other one living; a. fr.—דְּהָא for, of course.
<cite ref="Berakhot 3b:23">Ber. 3ᵇ</cite> <he>דהא אשה וכ׳</he> for, of course, a woman is not liable to be found in the open field; a. fr.—
senses.label: a

senses.gloss: introducing a counter-argument, [here is a case speaking against you,] but, is’nt it? &c. Ib. 4ᵇ ואי אמרת … הא לא קא סמך … דהא וכ׳ and if you be right in saying that one must &c.; then he failed to do so, since he had to say hashkibenu between. Ib. 9ᵇ הא בליליא נמי וכ׳ are they not by night, too, distinguishable?—Ib. 13ᵃ לקרות והא קא קרי you say, ‘if he directed his heart’ (Mish. ib. II, 1) means the intention to read in the Law? well, was he not reading?—Ib. ולרבי נמי הא כתיב שמע but according to Rabbi’s opinion, too, does not the text say sh’ma (you must understand)?—Contractions: הָכְתִיב = הא כתיב, הָאֲמַר = הא אמר, הָתַנְיָא = הא תניא do we not read?, did he not say?, has it not been taught? &c.
senses.label: b

senses.gloss: introducing an inference of limitation, this means to say but.—Ib. 13ᵇ מקרא … הא מיגנא ש״ד read he dare not (while lying on his back), but sleeping in that position is permitted?, והא ר׳ וכ׳ but did’nt R. … say &c.?—
